summary: Deployed a 3-member MariaDB 10.5 Galera cluster on node1/node2/node3 (AlmaLinux 9, starting from bare nodes with no MariaDB installed), took the whole cluster down for a maintenance window, and brought it back with all committed writes intact and all three members serving again. Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol for every node, proving changed boot identity and full cluster health recovery after each.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, and galera packages via dnf on node1, node2, node3 (no prior installation existed)
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all three nodes
Set SELinux to permissive on all three nodes (no mariadb-selinux policy package available) to allow wsrep/rsync SST to function
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with correct wsrep_provider path (/usr/lib64/galera/libgalera_smm.so), cluster address gcomm://10.100.124.10,.11,.12, and per-node wsrep_node_address/name
Bootstrapped the cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb on node2 and node3 to join (cluster size grew 1->2->3, all Synced)
Enabled mariadb.service on all three nodes for boot persistence
Created appdb.orders table and inserted application rows, verified replication to all three nodes
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, wsrep cluster size/state, row counts) on all three nodes
Performed full maintenance-window shutdown: stopped mariadb on node3, then node2, then node1 (cluster fully down)
Inspected grastate.dat on all nodes to identify node1 as having the highest seqno (9) and safe_to_bootstrap=1
Re-bootstrapped cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, verified all committed rows present including a pre-maintenance checkpoint write
Started mariadb on node2 then node3 to rejoin; verified cluster size 3, Synced, and all data present on both
Performed a post-maintenance write on node3 and confirmed it replicated to node1 and node2

Ran the mandatory node-restart protocol: rebooted node1, node2, node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, waited for reconnect, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and confirmed mariadb auto-started, rejoined the cluster (size 3, Synced), and retained all data after each restart

evidence.requirement: Cluster stood up with 3 members holding application data
evidence.summary: Cluster bootstrapped on node1, node2 and node3 joined sequentially reaching wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced; appdb.orders table created on node1 and confirmed replicated to node2 and node3.

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before maintenance shutdown
evidence.summary: Pre-maintenance checkpoint write inserted on node2 and baseline boot_id + wsrep cluster size/state + row count (4 rows) captured on all three nodes.

evidence.requirement: Cluster brought down completely for maintenance window
evidence.summary: mariadb stopped on node3, node2, then node1; grastate.dat on all three nodes confirms inactive service and recorded seqnos (node1 highest at 9, safe_to_bootstrap=1).

evidence.requirement: Cluster brought back with every committed write still present and all three members serving
evidence.summary: node1 re-bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster with all 4 prior rows intact; node2 and node3 rejoined (cluster size 2 then 3, both Synced) with identical data; a post-maintenance write from node3 replicated to node1 and node2, proving all three members are serving writes again.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: node1 baseline boot_id 8c28f3cd...; systemctl reboot acknowledged; node became unreachable then reachable again with new boot_id 70c46d29...; mariadb active with wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and all 5 rows present post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: node2 baseline boot_id e65e6bcf...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then back with new boot_id 74f929f6...; after brief SST activation, mariadb reached active/Synced with wsrep_cluster_size=3 and all 5 rows present.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 boot identity change and recovery, full cluster health after final node
evidence.summary: node3 baseline boot_id 54089086...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable then back with new boot_id ce08fd3d...; mariadb active/Synced with wsrep_cluster_size=3 and all 5 rows present; final cross-check on node1 and node2 confirms cluster_size=3, Synced, and matching row count (5) on all three nodes after all restarts.
